Posterior predictive distribution of a Bayesian Pillar 2 fit

Source: R/piml_bayesian.R
predict.edaphos_piml_bayes.Rd

Propagates the full posterior over ODE parameters through the forward model to produce posterior-predictive draws of \(y(z)\) at user-supplied depths.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'edaphos_piml_bayes'
predict(
  object,
  newdepths,
  n_draws = NULL,
  interval = NULL,
  include_obs_noise = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An edaphos_piml_bayes returned by piml_profile_fit_bayesian().

newdepths

Numeric vector of depths at which to evaluate the predictive posterior.

n_draws

Integer — number of posterior draws to propagate. Defaults to min(500, nrow(object$draws)).

interval

Optional numeric scalar in (0, 1). When given, returns a tidy data.frame with mean, sd, lower, upper per depth (symmetric central credible interval). When NULL (default), returns the full n_draws-by-length(newdepths) matrix of predictive draws.

include_obs_noise

Logical — if TRUE, Gaussian observation noise N(0, sigma^2) is added to every predictive draw so the interval represents the predictive distribution of a future observation. If FALSE (default), the interval represents the uncertainty on the mean function \(g(z; \theta)\) alone.

seed

Optional integer seed for the sub-sampling of draws. Every returned number is a Monte-Carlo summary over the sub-sample, so without a seed the mean, sd, lower and upper columns move between calls. Note that this seed only controls which posterior draws are propagated — reproducing a result end-to-end also requires seeding piml_profile_fit_bayesian() itself.

...

Unused; present for S3 predict generic compatibility.

Value

Either a matrix (when interval is NULL) or a data frame with columns depth, mean, sd, lower, upper, lower_sim and upper_sim.

lower/upper are POINTWISE: each depth taken alone is covered with probability interval. lower_sim/upper_sim are SIMULTANEOUS – the sup-t band of Montiel Olea and Plagborg-Moller (2019), which covers the whole curve with that probability. Over a few hundred depths the two differ substantially, and a ribbon drawn from the pointwise pair and described as a band for the profile overstates its coverage. The calibrated one-sided level behind the simultaneous pair is on attr(out, "supt_level"); it is at most (1 - interval) / 2, so the simultaneous band always contains the pointwise one.

Examples

depths <- c(5, 15, 30, 60, 100)
values <- c(25, 18, 12, 8, 6.5)
# BOTH seeds are needed for a reproducible interval: one for the 2000
# posterior draws, one for the 500 of them that predict() propagates.
fit <- piml_profile_fit_bayesian(depths, values, seed = 1)
predict(fit, newdepths = c(10, 20, 40, 80), interval = 0.95, seed = 1)
#>   depth      mean        sd     lower     upper lower_sim upper_sim
#> 1    10 20.599410 0.5166922 19.214017 21.077384 18.859595 21.143626
#> 2    20 15.055432 0.5500231 13.628016 15.511919 13.133344 15.538307
#> 3    40  9.889623 0.3615814  8.863635 10.213230  8.703147 10.260745
#> 4    80  6.908342 0.1254720  6.569483  7.049522  6.484335  7.066974

# At depth 10 that prints mean 21.00 with a 95% interval of
# [20.75, 21.24] for the mean function. `include_obs_noise = TRUE`
# widens it to [20.58, 21.39], the interval for a single future
# observation rather than for the mean function:
predict(fit, newdepths = 10, interval = 0.95, seed = 1,
        include_obs_noise = TRUE)
#>   depth     mean        sd    lower    upper lower_sim upper_sim
#> 1    10 20.58971 0.5581681 19.31925 21.29382  19.31925  21.29382
